singleJudge.finding: [geometry] The Sources dialog's single column of blocks has no consistent rhythm. Estimated from the ink and the line boxes, the gaps are about 8 px from the title to the description, about 12 px from the description to the inline error, about 16 px from the error to the nuget.org source item and about 14 px from that item to the Add Source footer. DS-GRID-2 (a) allows only 4 px inside a group and 8 px between groups, so same-role gaps between consecutive blocks differ and two of them are off that set.
singleJudge.reason: Single judge; contradicted by DS-GRID-2a@main-sources-error: gaps 8 (hard) (follow-up 2).

refuted.finding: The confirmation is not drawn over the sources dialog: behind the Remove nuget.org? layer the scrim covers only the Installed list and the empty details pane, and the NuGet sources dialog (drawn at about 375,297 to 824,505 in the main-sources capture of the same run) is missing, so the confirm floats with no parent layer, unlike a workbench modal stacked on its opener.
refuted.reason: The crop does show only the confirm over the scrimmed Installed page, but this is how the product is designed to work: primitives.css hides a covered layer ('.nuiget-dialog-layer[data-covered] { visibility: hidden }', 'one scrim, one box', UX-P3.6). DECISIONS 2026-11-07 judges this cell against main-installed-details as the page beneath, and that artboard draws no sources dialog. The measurements agree with one scrim: DS-DIVIDER-5 'scrim rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) over #1f1f1f → #101010' and '[aria] main-sources-remove-dialog: 64 nodes, equal'.

refuted.finding: The confirm layer has no close action in its top-end corner, while the product's own sources dialog draws a codicon close button there (about 787,311 in main-sources) and the workbench's modal dialog keeps its close action on every dialog.
refuted.reason: The crop at 770,321 54x54 shows plain dialog background, but no artboard, spec or rule gives a ConfirmDialog a close action: the interaction model specifies 'Remove / Cancel, focus on Cancel' with Escape closing (design-system row for Dialog, ConfirmDialog), so the missing close action is a design choice and not a defect (rubric §6, taste with no artboard element).

refuted.finding: The Remove confirmation shows with no Sources dialog under it, though the interaction model specifies the ConfirmDialog "over the sources dialog". The sibling capture main-sources.dark-modern.1200.png draws the Sources dialog (title "NuGet sources", the nuget.org row with its Remove button, Add Source...) at about x 375–825, y 297–505. That dialog is taller than this confirm (y 328–474), so if it were mounted underneath, its top and bottom bands would show above and below the confirm. They do not: only the scrimmed Installed page shows. The opener the focus should return to, and the context of the destructive action, are missing from the state.
refuted.reason: The sources dialog is visibly absent above and below the confirm (y 328–474), but the product hides it on purpose: the covered layer is set to 'visibility: hidden' ('one scrim, one box', UX-P3.6). The ConfirmDialog is still stacked over the mounted sources dialog. The artboard this cell is judged against (main-installed-details as the page beneath, DECISIONS 2026-11-07) draws no sources dialog, so nothing is missing from it, and the ARIA snapshot reads '64 nodes, equal' to the adopted golden.

refuted.finding: The dialog's description still explains the Remove action ("Remove deletes a source from the file that declares it.") while the empty state has no source and no Remove control, so it describes a control this state does not draw. The empty message below it already names the condition.
refuted.reason: The crop shows the dialog's fixed description, "Sources of the selected project's config files. Remove deletes a source from the file that declares it.", which is correct sentence-case copy ending in a period (DS-COPY-3 hard: "1 end with a full stop"). The empty state is present (DS-STATE-1 hard: "present: source-settings-empty; missing: none"), and the ARIA snapshot reads "63 nodes, equal". The artboard (main-installed-details) does not draw this dialog. The finding cites no rule, so under rubric §6 a correct description that also mentions a feature this state does not show is taste, not a defect.

refuted.finding: Inside the sources dialog the inline error's text column starts at x≈415 while the source item's name and URL start at x≈418–419, though the error glyph (x≈393) and the item's check box (x≈392) share one start edge. The 16 px glyph and the 18 px check box each take the same gap, so the two text columns end up 3 px apart. A built-in dialog keeps message and list text on one column; the artboard draws no dialog to compare with.
refuted.reason: In the crop, the stems of the left-most letters start at x=417 for the error's 'N' (rows 390-395) and x=418 for the item's 'h' (rows 438-439), which is within 1 px. That gap is the same 1 px side-bearing spread that 'h' (418) and 'n' (419) show inside the item's own text, so the claimed 3 px offset is not visible.
